8
A snooker ball has a mass of 200 g. It hits the cushion of a snooker table and rebounds along its
original path.
The ball arrives at the cushion with a speed of 14.0 m s–1 and then leaves it with a speed of
7.0 m s–1. The ball and the cushion are in contact for a time of 0.60 s.
What is the average force exerted on the ball by the cushion?
A
1.4 N
B
2.3 N
C
4.2 N
D
7.0 N

hints: Notice the ball rebounds along its original path, so take one direction as positive and the opposite direction as negative when finding change in velocity.
Convert the $200 \text{ g}$ mass to $0.20 \text{ kg}$ and combine the $14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ arrival speed and $7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ rebound speed to get the total change in momentum.
Use impulse $F\Delta t = \Delta p = m\Delta v$ with $\Delta t = 0.60 \text{ s}$ to find the average force magnitude.
walkthrough: Choose a positive direction, for example away from the cushion. Then initial velocity $u = -14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and final velocity $v = +7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Convert mass to SI units: $m = 200 \text{ g} = 0.20 \text{ kg}$.
Find the change in velocity: $\Delta v = v - u = 7.0 - (-14.0) = 21.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. Rebound means the magnitudes add.
Find the change in momentum: $\Delta p = m\Delta v = 0.20 \times 21.0 = 4.2 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Use $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$ for average force: $F = 4.2 / 0.60 = 7.0 \text{ N}$ with units of $\text{kg m s}^{-2} = \text{N}$.

A.explanation: This is the change in momentum if the speeds are subtracted, $0.20 \times 7.0 = 1.4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, not divided by time to give force.

B.explanation: This uses $14.0 - 7.0 = 7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for the velocity change, ignoring that rebound reverses direction so the changes add.

C.explanation: This is the magnitude of the change in momentum, $0.20 \times 21.0 = 4.2 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, before dividing by the $0.60 \text{ s}$ contact time.

D.explanation: With velocity reversal the change in momentum is $0.20 \times 21.0$ divided by $0.60 \text{ s}$, giving $7.0 \text{ N}$.
